title: Trigonometry
description: Radians, the unit circle, sine, cosine, tangent and trigonometric equations.
html:
📐 Trigonometry

1. Radians and the unit circle

$$x = \alpha \cdot \frac{\pi}{180°}, \qquad \pi \text{ rad} = 180°$$

$$P(\varphi) = (\cos\varphi,\ \sin\varphi), \qquad \tan\varphi = \frac{\sin\varphi}{\cos\varphi}$$

$\varphi$$0$$\frac{\pi}{6}$$\frac{\pi}{4}$$\frac{\pi}{3}$$\frac{\pi}{2}$
$\sin$$0$$\frac{1}{2}$$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$1$
$\cos$$1$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}$$\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}$$\frac{1}{2}$$0$

2. Symmetries

$$\sin(-x) = -\sin x, \ \cos(-x) = \cos x, \ \sin(\pi - x) = \sin x, \ \cos(\pi - x) = -\cos x$$

Periodicity: $\sin$, $\cos$ have period $2\pi$, $\tan$ has period $\pi$.

3. Graphs

$$f(x) = A\sin\big(B(x - C)\big) + D: \quad \text{amplitude } |A|, \ \text{period } \tfrac{2\pi}{|B|}$$

$\tan$ has poles at $\frac{\pi}{2} + k\pi$. Triangle: $\sin = \frac{\text{opp.}}{\text{hyp.}}$, $\cos = \frac{\text{adj.}}{\text{hyp.}}$.

4. Identities

$$\sin^2 x + \cos^2 x = 1$$

$$\sin(a + b) = \sin a \cos b + \cos a \sin b, \qquad \cos(a + b) = \cos a \cos b - \sin a \sin b$$

$$\sin 2x = 2\sin x\cos x, \qquad \cos 2x = 1 - 2\sin^2 x = 2\cos^2 x - 1$$

5. Equations and triangles

$\sin x = c$: principal value $\arcsin c$ and reflection $\pi - \arcsin c$, then $+2k\pi$. $\tan x = c$: $\arctan c + k\pi$.

$$\frac{a}{\sin\alpha} = \frac{b}{\sin\beta} = \frac{c}{\sin\gamma}, \qquad c^2 = a^2 + b^2 - 2ab\cos\gamma$$
